summary: Ribbon overlaid on the corner of cards or images (“Beta”, “New”, “-20%”, “Sold out”): wraps the content in a positioned container and overlays a short label as a diagonal band, bookmark, or flag.
whenToUse: Highlight a card in a grid (sold-out event, new course, discount).
Mark a preview or image with a short, highly visible status.
whenNotToUse: Inline labels in text or next to a heading: use Badge or StageLabel.
Counts or dots on avatars and icons: use IndicatorBadge.
Long information or information essential to understanding the card: put it in the content; the ribbon truncates long text.

props.name: label
props.description: Short ribbon text; it is real text, read before the content.

props.name: children
props.description: Content the ribbon is overlaid on (card, image…).

props.name: variant
props.description: Diagonal band in the corner, vertical bookmark with a V-shaped tail, or flag that protrudes from the edge.

props.name: position
props.description: Logical corner: automatically mirrored in RTL.

props.name: tone
props.description: Color; brand uses the accent gradient.

accessibility: The ribbon text is not hidden: it comes before the content in the DOM, so screen readers read it first.
The ribbon does not intercept clicks (pointer-events: none): links and buttons underneath remain usable.
Don’t rely on the ribbon alone for essential information (e.g. “Sold out”): repeat it near the action, for example by disabling the button with explicit text.
In forced-colors mode the ribbon uses a system border instead of background and gradient; in print it keeps colors and border.
responsive: The container takes the width of the content; corner and bookmark are clipped to the rounded corners.
The corner variant truncates text longer than ~10 characters with an ellipsis: prefer short labels.
customization: Tokens: --dc-gradient-accent (brand), --dc-color-accent-default, feedback colors and --dc-color-surface-inverse for the other tones, --dc-look-radius-container for clipping.

The container uses overflow: hidden and a border-radius equal to --dc-look-radius-container (overridable via className/style); the banner variant uses visible overflow because it protrudes from the edge.
commonMistakes: Using long text (“Registration closed on March 12”): the ribbon is designed for one or two words.
Wrapping an element that has outer margins: clipping follows the container, not the card.
Using the banner variant inside a container with hidden overflow: the flag gets clipped.
